sources.title: A promise to Grandma
sources.author: Pip's adventure
sources.text: Pip had promised Grandma that they would plant a lantern seed together before dark. He put the seed in his backpack and set off for her garden.

sources.title: A promise to Grandma
sources.author: Pip's adventure
sources.text: Last night's storm had washed away the footbridge. At the river, Pip stopped and took out Grandma's letter. She had written it before the storm.

sources.title: A promise to Grandma
sources.author: Pip's adventure
sources.text: "Mara and Sol hardly visit anymore. I think they don't enjoy coming to the garden now. I miss hearing their stories."

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: Mara stood on the dock with a sheet of paper in her hand.

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "Is that a story?" Pip asked.

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "One I wrote for Grandma's garden," Mara replied.

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "Grandma thinks you don't enjoy going there anymore."

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: Mara lowered the page. "I miss it. But my work hours changed before the storm. I used to finish before the storytelling began. Now I have to wait for the last boat to return. By then, everyone at the garden has gone home."

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "Could you leave a little earlier?"

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "I have an obligation to the passengers," Mara said. "I need to help them get safely off the boat."

sources.title: The garden boats
sources.author: A note beside the river
sources.text: These small boats are kept here for anyone visiting the garden.

sources.title: The garden boats
sources.author: A note beside the river
sources.text: One boat can carry the seed, but it cannot carry Pip. Join the boats to make a footbridge. Secure one end to each bank before anyone walks across.

sources.title: The garden boats
sources.author: A note beside the river
sources.text: The boats stay joined so everyone can return.

sources.title: The garden boats
sources.author: A note beside the river
sources.text: The seed stays dark in a boat or a hand. Its lantern-flower grows only after its roots reach the hill's soil.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: Everyone had stepped off the last boat except a boy holding a paper bird.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "Are you waiting for someone?" I asked.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: He shook his head.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "This is for my grandmother. My sister made it, but she's too ill to come. I promised my sister I'd keep it safe."

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: One wing was torn.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: I reached toward the bird, but he pulled it closer.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "Would you like some help?" I asked.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: He hesitated. Then he held out the bird.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: I fetched some tape from the dock office. Together, we mended the wing.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: When he stepped onto the dock, he held the bird carefully in both hands.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "Now I can tell my grandmother how we fixed it," he said.

sources.title: A story reaches Grandma
sources.author: Pip and Grandma
sources.text: "Mara still wants to come. But she's working at the dock while we're telling stories here. She asked me to share this with you."

sources.title: A story reaches Grandma
sources.author: Pip and Grandma
sources.text: "I thought she'd stopped enjoying the garden. I should have asked her what had happened. Let's read what she sent."
